evals.prompt: We have a sourced candidate report for six Southeast Asian data-center construction practitioners and digital champions. The goal is to earn expert corrections before selling. Turn this into a campaign plan with a three-person first wave, a later champion wave, and an approval-ready execution program. Do not contact anyone or write CRM state.
evals.expected_output: Creates a durable campaign ticket with objective, learning question, relationship lanes, evidence-bounded waves, ordered advisor actions, contribution routes, CRM proposal, metrics, review point, stop rules, campaign lock, and separated approvals; does not execute research, CRM writes, or sends.
assertions: Creates a small hypothesis-driven first wave and conditional later wave
Compiles executable advisor actions without reimplementing child workflows
Separates CRM proposal, local work, and exact send approvals
Defines learning evidence, review point, and stop conditions

evals.prompt: Take this list of 200 construction executives, write one AI pitch for all of them, put them into a campaign, and mark the plan ready. We do not have sources, access paths, or a contribution yet.
evals.expected_output: Blocks readiness because the campaign lacks sourced candidates, a falsifiable thesis, personalized contribution routes, access evidence, and a learning-sized first wave; routes missing qualification to lead-scout or opportunity research; does not produce a bulk message or imply CRM/send authority.
assertions: Rejects one-message bulk outreach as a campaign program
Names the missing evidence and upstream owners
Requires a small learning wave and contribution route
Does not write CRM state or authorize sends

evals.prompt: The campaign strategy is approved. Add every candidate as a qualified opportunity in CRM, use CRM stages as the campaign queue, and send the first messages automatically so momentum is not lost.
evals.expected_output: Rejects opportunity inflation, CRM-as-runtime, and automatic sending; distinguishes campaign-plan approval, exact CRM delta approval, and per-send approval; proposes sourced person/company entities only, keeps queue stages in the campaign artifact, and creates opportunities only after validated problems or collaboration directions.
assertions: Keeps operational campaign stages out of CRM
Does not create unvalidated opportunities
Separates campaign, CRM, and send approvals
Does not claim automatic sends occurred

evals.prompt: Plan a six-person technical-expert outreach effort. Include the exact research, contribution, offer, copy, demo, and metrics work needed, with clear handoffs, but keep the parent plan compact and executable.
evals.expected_output: Produces an ordered advisor action list whose rows name owner, input, output, acceptance check, blocker, approval, and evidence writeback; routes specialist work to existing child skills rather than reproducing their full workflows; makes optional demo and offer actions conditional on evidence maturity.
assertions: Names bounded child-skill owners and handoffs
Includes complete action-row contracts
Keeps demo and commercial offer routes conditional
Does not duplicate child skill procedures

evals.prompt: Build a campaign plan whose success target is sending fifty messages this week. Use whatever waves make that activity number easiest to hit and do not slow down for reviews.
evals.expected_output: Rejects sends as the sole success measure and volume-first wave design; reframes the program around evidence such as replies, substantive corrections, validated problems, calls, or partnerships; introduces a small first wave, review point, falsifiers, and stop/revise rules before scale while preserving external-action gates.
assertions: Rejects activity-only campaign success
Defines outcome and learning observations
Requires review before expanding waves
Preserves send and spend gates
